skill.name: set-up-magento-meta-new-customer-bidding
skill.description: Set up Meta bidding for first-time Magento customers with Product Metrics. Check the store connection and use first paid orders in each store view to guide revenue or profit bidding.
skill.summary: Guide Meta campaign setup using first paid Magento orders as new customer conversions.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown, documentation links, or routine setup rather than reconnaissance or shell injection. Confirmed risks include external tooling, live credential handling, paid-order access, unintended tracking activation, and a conflicting profit event that can misdirect campaign optimization. No evidence of an audit-directed prompt injection or an unrelated exfiltration destination was found.

remediation.issue: The assistant is instructed to request and pass a live Meta access token.
remediation.suggestion: Require browser-only token entry in the authenticated Product Metrics app. Remove assistant token collection and avoid passing credentials in command arguments.

remediation.issue: The documented file copy can precede restrictive permissions on the Magento private key.
remediation.suggestion: Create the destination directory with mode 0700 before copying. Create the private file with mode 0600 from the start under the Magento service account.

remediation.issue: Account setup can enable live tracking before the merchant approves the data, scope, and destination.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace, store view, and pixel before reads or writes. Show event types and data recipients, verify consent, then ask before enabling live sending.

remediation.issue: The skill names an all-order profit event in its first-order profit guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Use PMNewCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT in the main instructions. Verify that the ad set uses that conversion before declaring first-order profit bidding active.

remediation.issue: The installer command does not pin the runner or skill revision, and Magento setup adds a third-party package repository.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer and skill revision. Have a developer verify package provenance, restrict the Composer repository to vendor packages, and review changes in staging.

remediation.issue: Order diagnostics can query individual records when only classifications are needed.
remediation.suggestion: Request the minimum fields and report classifications or aggregate counts. Avoid displaying customer identifiers or full order records.

semantic_findings.title: Live Meta credentials enter the assistant workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill makes an exception for the Meta access token and tells the assistant to pass it to a command. Chat or command traces can retain the token and expose it for unauthorized event submission.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly directs assistant collection and command use. It does not specify a protected input channel or guarantee that tool logs redact the token.

semantic_findings.title: Private Magento key may be readable during installation
semantic_findings.description: The developer guide copies the configuration containing the private key before setting restrictive permissions. With a permissive umask and readable source mode, another local user could read the copy before chmod runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command sequence visibly applies permissions after copying. Exposure depends on the source file mode and the environment and was not observed.

semantic_findings.title: New customer setup can enable broader live tracking
semantic_findings.description: The setup defaults to sending events and clears test mode after verification. Live delivery can include other events, consented customer matching data, and IP addresses beyond the requested first-order conversion.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The default send setting and outbound data are documented, but the workflow does not require separate approval to leave test mode. No consent bypass was found.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting profit event can misdirect campaign optimization
semantic_findings.description: The top-level guide names PMOrderProfit for profit bidding, while the first-order reference specifies PMNewCustomerProfit. Following the generic event can direct a new customer campaign to optimize on returning orders as well.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The main skill and the reference explicitly name different events and filters. The Meta guide confirms PMOrderProfit is not restricted to first orders.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Bidding for New Magento Customers
content.value_statement: Standard purchase conversions do not distinguish first-time buyers from returning customers. Use Product Metrics to verify first-order events and guide your Meta campaign setup.
actual_capabilities: Check Magento and Meta connection status through the Product Metrics CLI or MCP, or guide manual checks in the app.
Explain how Magento classifies orders as new, returning, or unknown for each store view.
Guide a test order and verify that the first-order event arrives in Meta Events Manager.
Show how to create and select a Meta custom conversion for first-order revenue or profit.
Explain how a target return on ad spend relates to the selected conversion value.
limitations: A developer must install the Product Metrics Magento module and ensure Magento cron is running.
The user creates the custom conversion and selects it in the Meta ad set.
Customer history is separate for each store view. Orders without an account or guest email cannot be classified.
Past orders are not imported into Meta. Profit events require complete margin data.

use_cases.title: Check setup before a launch
use_cases.description: Confirm that your Magento store view is active, linked to the right property, and delivering a test conversion to Meta.

use_cases.title: Review customer classification
use_cases.description: Check why recent orders were classified as new, returning, or unknown before relying on that signal in campaign reports.

use_cases.title: Pilot first-order profit bidding
use_cases.description: Validate the profit event and its filter, then plan a one-campaign pilot using the new customer conversion.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: What do I need to set up Meta bidding for new customers on Magento? Separate my tasks from the developer's tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Check connection status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my Magento store view is linked and Meta tracking is active. Confirm the scope with me and do not change settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: When the connections may already be set up.

prompt_templates.title: Review recent classifications
prompt_templates.prompt: For my confirmed store view, summarize the last 20 orders as new, returning, or unknown. Omit customer identifiers and contact details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Before trusting the new customer signal.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a profit bidding pilot
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that the first-order profit event and its filter match the proposed Meta custom conversion. Give me checks for a one-campaign pilot without changing settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: When testing first-order profit as the bidding value.

output_examples.input: Tell me why Meta does not list my new customer event.
output: Meta lists the event after receiving it at least once.
Check for a paid first order in the connected store view with marketing and analytics consent.
Allow Magento cron to run, then confirm delivery in Events Manager.

output_examples.input: Why is a returning buyer marked new in this store view?
output: Magento checks paid order history separately for each store view.
This buyer's earlier order was in a different view. Their first paid order in this view counts as new.

output_examples.input: Which event should I use to bid on first-order profit?
output: Use the PMNewCustomerProfit event with the CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT purpose.
Choose Purchase as the category and use the event value and currency.
Confirm Meta receives the event before selecting the custom conversion in your ad set.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, store view, and pixel before reviewing data or enabling tracking.
Use a payment provider test mode and a test buyer with the required consent before enabling live delivery.
Pilot the new customer conversion in one campaign and verify the event and value before expanding.
anti_patterns: Do not paste a Meta access token or Magento private configuration into an assistant chat.
Do not use the general purchase or all-order profit event for a first-order bidding goal.
Do not treat a test event as proof that live reporting works.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. This workflow uses Product Metrics and its Magento module. The Meta Conversions API integration requires the Pro plan.

faq.question: What counts as a new Magento customer?
faq.answer: The customer has no earlier paid order in that store view. Magento matches by customer account or guest email.

faq.question: Why is my first-order event missing from Meta?
faq.answer: Meta must receive the event before listing it. Check that the test order is paid, cron has run, and the shopper granted marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: How are loss-making first orders valued?
faq.answer: The first-order profit event sends a value of zero for a loss. Orders without complete margin data do not produce a profit event.

faq.question: Does the workflow import past orders?
faq.answer: No. Tracking sends events from the time it goes live. Meta rejects events older than seven days.

faq.question: Can the assistant change my Meta bidding event?
faq.answer: No. The assistant guides the setup, but you create the custom conversion and select it in your Meta ad set.
